text:
Tim Stützle has 11 goals in 21 games, and the finish is doing a lot of the work. His chances add up to 6.76 expected goals (the quality of his shots), and he's shooting 22% against 18% last season, well above the top of our range for him. That's the kind of rate that rarely lasts, even for a skilled shooter. His last ten games brought 10 points against 11.8 expected, so the overall production has already settled back toward normal.

What's encouraging for Ottawa is underneath the goals. The Senators hold 56.9% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, even though the shot attempts are roughly even, which means the chances they get are the better ones. He's also been more physical than his reputation, with 45 hits. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 62% of his entries last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him drawing more penalties than he takes. The flip side, per Evolving-Hockey, was defense: bottom 4% among forwards in chances allowed. We'd watch the goal pace cool and the playmaking carry more of the load.
